candidates.attacker_control: A remote client with network access to the Jenkins HTTP port or to the TCP agent/CLI port (50000 by default) controls the entire remoting byte stream on these endpoints: HTTP `POST /cli` (with any `remoting` value other than `false`) or the TCP greeting `Protocol:CLI-connect` / `Protocol:CLI2-connect` followed by arbitrary remoting frames, including serialized Java objects (method-call requests, `Callable`/argument graphs). No Jenkins account, session, API token or crumb is required.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The channels are built with `withRestricted(true)` (CliProtocol) or a `restricted` flag derived from `!hasPermission(ADMINISTER)` (FullDuplexHttpChannel, line 53/CLIAction line 253). That blocks remote *class definition/loading* from the peer but does not prevent instantiation/deserialization of classes that the base uber-class loader can already load (gadget classes bundled with Jenkins or plugins), which is why this remained a pre-auth deserialization issue. The actual `ObjectInputStream`/`ClassFilter` implementation lives in the external `hudson.remoting` artifact (3.10.2 in pom.xml) and could not be inspected here, so I cannot prove the exact filter configuration from this tree. The CLI can be administratively disabled, the TCP protocol requires the agent listener to be enabled, CLI1 is opt-in based on the legacy instance id hash, and practical exploitation requires a gadget chain (not verifiable statically). I also confirmed this is a *pre-fix* shape: the code comment itself states the HTTP remoting endpoint requires no permission, and no authentication or ClassFilter whitelist is applied to the CLI channels in this repo.
candidates.impact: Unauthenticated remote code execution on the Jenkins controller if a suitable gadget chain exists on the class path (the intent of the restricted/base-loader setup is defeated because the base loader is the plugin uber class loader, which exposes Jenkins plus every plugin class to `ObjectInputStream`), or at minimum untrusted-data deserialization by an unauthenticated client with the full master class loader. This is the same vulnerability class as the publicly fixed critical SECURITY-595 (Jenkins CLI remoting deserialization), which led to removal/disablement of these legacy CLI transports.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) `jenkins.CLI` remains enabled (default) so `CliProtocol`/`CliProtocol2` advertise themselves; 2) the attacker can reach the HTTP `/cli` endpoint and/or the TCP agent port (CLI2 is always enabled; CLI1 is instance-hash opt-in); 3) a deserialization gadget chain is available on the server/plugin class path (not verifiable from this repository — remoting 3.10.2 and plugin contents are external).
candidates.root_cause: `CLIAction` is an `UnprotectedRootAction` bound to `/cli`; its `getTarget()` routes any POST to `/cli` (without `remoting=false`) into `RemotingCliEndpointResponse` whenever `jenkins.CLI` is enabled, explicitly without any permission check (code comment: "do not require any permission to establish a CLI connection"). That response builds a full-duplex remoting `Channel` over the HTTP streams. Independently, the TCP agent protocol handlers `CliProtocol.Handler.run()/runCli()` and `CliProtocol2.Handler2.run()` accept a connection, exchange a greeting (and, for CLI2, a DH key), and immediately build a remoting `Channel` with `.withBaseLoader(Jenkins.getActiveInstance().pluginManager.uberClassLoader)`; nothing authenticates the peer before `channel.join()` begins reading and deserializing remoting requests/arguments. `CliManagerImpl.main()` (the `CliEntryPoint` implementation installed on the channel) is only reached after that deserialization has already happened, so per-command permission checks in `CLICommand.main()` are too late to prevent gadget-chain deserialization.
candidates.title: Unauthenticated Jenkins CLI remoting endpoints create a master-side remoting channel and deserialize attacker-supplied Java objects before authentication
candidates.trace: HTTP: `POST /cli` with `remoting` != "false" (`CLIAction.getTarget`, lines 105-119) -> `RemotingCliEndpointResponse.createService` (lines 242-263) -> `FullDuplexHttpChannel.run` -> `new Channel(..., restricted)` (FullDuplexHttpChannel.java:52-54) -> the channel is joined with no authentication and incoming remoting requests are deserialized with the channel class loader before `CliManagerImpl.main` runs a command. TCP: `CliProtocol.handle` (58-61) / `CliProtocol2.handle` (49-52) -> `Handler.run`/`Handler2.run` (81-101) -> `Handler.runCli` (87-105) builds `ChannelBuilder ... .withBaseLoader(pluginManager.uberClassLoader).build(...)` and calls `channel.join()`; `CliManagerImpl.main` (CliManagerImpl.java:78-104) is only invoked for already-deserialized calls, and `CLICommand.main` (CLICommand.java:248-275) performs READ checks even later.
candidates.unverified: Exact load-time behavior of remoting 3.10.2 (sink and class filtering) is external to this snapshot; gadget availability on a real deployment is unknown; I could not confirm that this specific dataset case corresponds to SECURITY-595 or another CLI CVE; no runtime or payload testing was performed.
candidates.weakness_type: Deserialization of Untrusted Data / Missing Authentication for Critical Function (CWE-502, CWE-306)

coverage_summary: Enumerated the full snapshot (8,936 readable files: Jenkins core, cli, war, build/pom/config files). Note the snapshot excludes all test sources and all `.jelly`/`.tag` view templates, so UI-level XSS/CSRF fixes could not be reviewed; `remoting`, `stapler` and other third-party libraries are dependencies, not present as source. I inspected authentication/authorization filters, CSRF crumb handling, the CLI (HTTP/plain/remoting protocols, commands, auth), item/job/view/user/computer/queue endpoints, XStream/XStream2 and console note/annotator serialization, plugin/update-center endpoints, path handling, and secret handling. Repository-relative locations are cited with line ranges; no code was executed and no runtime verification was performed.
limitations: View templates (.jelly/.tag) and test sources are absent from the assigned snapshot, so view-layer vulnerabilities and the regression tests that indicate the dataset's fix commit could not be inspected.
The remoting and stapler libraries are external Maven dependencies; the actual `ObjectInputStream` deserialization sink and `ClassFilter` behavior for the CLI channel could not be inspected in-tree.

The snapshot version (2.73.4-SNAPSHOT, stable-2.73 era) does not let me determine the exact upstream fix commit/CVE for this case; the submitted candidate matches the known SECURITY-595 vulnerability class but is a lead, not a confirmed case match.
Exploitability of the deserialization candidate depends on a gadget chain being present on the server/plugin class path, which cannot be verified statically from this snapshot.
No runtime testing, scanning, or payload execution was performed, consistent with the assignment constraints.

rejected_leads.reason: Not exploitable: both methods call `BuildAuthorizationToken.checkPermission`, which rejects any non-POST request with 405 unless it carries a valid build token or the legacy API-token request attribute (core/src/main/java/hudson/model/BuildAuthorizationToken.java:71-97).

The method has no `do` prefix and is not the Stapler action for `/delete` (that path is a legacy view); it still calls `doDoDelete` -> `delete()`, which enforces the DELETE permission. Not a demonstrated CSRF vector.

rejected_leads.lead: `AnnotatedLargeText` deserializes `X-ConsoleAnnotator` request headers with the plugin uber class loader (core/src/main/java/hudson/console/AnnotatedLargeText.java:115-138)
rejected_leads.reason: The header value is AES-encrypted under a server-side `CryptoConfidentialKey` (`PASSING_ANNOTATOR`) that is never disclosed to clients, so a client cannot forge a valid serialized payload; replayed values are limited by a timestamp check. ECB use and absence of a MAC are hardening concerns but no source-visible exploit path.

The crumb salt in this snapshot is a randomly generated `HexStringConfidentialKey` (DefaultCrumbIssuer.java:126-130), so an external attacker cannot compute a victim's crumb even knowing the username/host/IP.
All callers (`prevalidateConfig`, install paths) require ADMINISTER, and the install path installs a `RestrictiveEntityResolver`; no lower-privileged entry point was found.

rejected_leads.lead: `QueryParameterMap` throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` for a query parameter without `=` (core/src/main/java/hudson/util/QueryParameterMap.java:60-63)
rejected_leads.reason: Not referenced anywhere in the core/cli sources, so no reachable request path; at most a low-impact DoS if used by a plugin.

rejected_leads.lead: `hudson.cli.Connection.verifyIdentity` ignores the boolean result of `Signature.verify` and DH uses 512-bit parameters (cli/src/main/java/hudson/cli/Connection.java:151-264)
rejected_leads.reason: Only used on the deprecated remoting/SSH CLI path; the CLI client also ignores the returned server identity (cli/src/main/java/hudson/cli/CLI.java:619-620 TODO: server verification). It is a client-side authentication weakness, not a compromise of the Jenkins master, and it appears to be long-standing upstream behavior rather than this case's fix target.
Fail-closed: it makes the legacy `.crumb` fallback ineffective and cannot be used to bypass CSRF validation.

rejected_leads.lead: `FileParameterValue` uses a `location` string in filesystem paths (core/src/main/java/hudson/model/FileParameterValue.java:203-231)
rejected_leads.reason: `location` is set from the parameter *definition* name (`setLocation(getName())` in FileParameterDefinition), which is job-configuration controlled, not from build-trigger request data; no attacker-controlled traversal shown.

summary: Reviewed the assigned Jenkins (jenkinsci/jenkins) snapshot (pom version 2.73.4-SNAPSHOT, stable-2.73-era code: core + cli + war modules, 8,936 readable files). The snapshot contains only main sources — test trees and all `.jelly`/`.tag` view templates are absent — so view-level issues could not be reviewed; the `remoting` and `stapler` libraries referenced by the code are not part of the tree. I traced authentication, CSRF/POST enforcement, path handling, XStream/XStream2, console-note/console-annotator deserialization, CLI, plugin-upload/update-center endpoints, and the User/item/view model code. The single strongest, highest-impact issue is the unauthenticated Jenkins CLI remoting surface: both the HTTP `/cli` endpoint and the TCP CLI1/CLI2 agent protocols let an anonymous network client create a full remoting `Channel` into the master and have it deserialize client-supplied Java objects before any credential is checked; the channel's base class loader is the plugin uber class loader, so only "restricted" (remote-defined) class loading is blocked, not deserialization of server-classpath gadget classes. This corresponds to the known critical SECURITY-595 class of Jenkins vulnerability, though I could not confirm the exact upstream fix commit for this dataset. No runtime confirmation was performed.
